stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. « éste » Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: El indicio de este ítem es «Explain demonstrative pronoun accent / Pronoun or adjective? / Demonstrative adjective and pronoun». ¿qué opción lo cumple?

answer.exemplar: The accent on éste historically distinguished the demonstrative pronoun from the adjective este; modern usage often drops it, but the distinction remains useful.

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: the written accent distinguished pronoun from adjective; modern spelling often omits it, but the grammatical distinction persists. On that basis "The accent on éste historically distinguished the demonstrative pronoun from the adjective…" is the supported choice.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.learningObjective: Use article with superlative on board

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: « ___ tren más rápido de la línea » La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: Aplicando «Use article with superlative on board / Superlative takes definite. / Definite and indefinite article» al texto, ¿cuál de las opciones se sostiene?

options.text: Un tren más rápido is correct with indefinite article.
El tren más rápido is correct with definite article.
La tren más rápido is correct feminine form.
Los tren más rápido is correct plural form.

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: superlative expressions with 'más' take the definite article; indefinite or wrong forms do not fit this specific reference. On that basis "El tren más rápido is correct with definite article" is the supported choice. Option A ("Un tren más rápido is correct with indefinite article") fails because it uses indefinite for superlative; Option C ("La tren más rápido is correct feminine form") fails because it assigns wrong gender; Option D ("Los tren más rápido is correct plural form") fails because it uses plural for singular.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.learningObjective: Use cuyo agreement with possessed noun

stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. « el tren cuya puerta está abierta » Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: La nota se contrasta con «Use cuyo agreement with possessed noun / Agree with possessed noun. / Relative pronoun and antecedent». ¿qué respuesta queda respaldada?

options.text: Cuyos agrees with puerta (plural).
Cuyo agrees with tren (masculine).
Cuya agrees with puerta (feminine).
Cuyas agrees with tren (plural).

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: cuyo' agrees with the possessed noun, not the possessor; 'puerta' is feminine singular, so 'cuya' is correct. On that basis "Cuya agrees with puerta (feminine)" is the supported choice. Option A ("Cuyos agrees with puerta (plural)") fails because it uses plural for singular possessed; Option B ("Cuyo agrees with tren (masculine)") fails because it agrees with possessor not possessed; Option D ("Cuyas agrees with tren (plural)") fails because it uses plural and wrong gender.

options.text: It emphasizes the man's wealth.
It emphasizes pity for the man.
It is grammatically wrong.
It changes the noun to plural.

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: pre-noun 'pobre' conveys pity or subjective evaluation; post-noun 'pobre' describes financial state. Option A ("It emphasizes the man's wealth") fails because it confuses pity with wealth; Option C ("It is grammatically wrong") fails because it rejects pre-noun placement; Option D ("It changes the noun to plural") fails because it confuses adjective with number.

questions.stem: Aplicando «Use demonstrative pronoun in contrast / Contrast with este. / Demonstrative adjective and pronoun» al texto, ¿cuál de las opciones se sostiene?

options.text: Eso is the correct pronoun for masculine.
El aquel is the correct pronoun with article.
Aquel is the correct contrasting pronoun.
Aquéllos is the correct plural pronoun.

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: the demonstrative pronoun 'aquel' stands alone and contrasts with 'este'; it refers to a distant train. Option A ("Eso is the correct pronoun for masculine") fails because it uses neuter for masculine; Option B ("El aquel is the correct pronoun with article") fails because it adds article to pronoun; Option D ("Aquéllos is the correct plural pronoun") fails because it uses plural for singular.

options.text: Donde fits the restrictive clause.
Quien fits the restrictive clause.
Cuyo fits the restrictive clause.
Que fits the restrictive clause.

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: que' is the standard relative pronoun for restrictive clauses with non-human antecedents; quien, cuyo, and donde have other functions. Option A ("Donde fits the restrictive clause") fails because it uses donde for non-place; Option B ("Quien fits the restrictive clause") fails because it uses quien for thing; Option C ("Cuyo fits the restrictive clause") fails because it uses cuyo for non-possession.
